section_179_cap_2025.verbatim_quote: Public Law 119-21 Section 70306 increases the Section 179 aggregate dollar limitation to $2,500,000 for property placed in service in taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024.

superseded_values.label: Pre-OBBBA 2025 Section 179 cap ($1,250,000)
superseded_values.reason: Superseded retroactively for tax years beginning after Dec 31, 2024 by P.L. 119-21 Section 70306.

section_179_phaseout_2025.verbatim_quote: Public Law 119-21 Section 70306 raises the Section 179 investment phaseout threshold to $4,000,000 for property placed in service in taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024.

superseded_values.label: Pre-OBBBA 2025 Section 179 phaseout ($3,130,000)
superseded_values.reason: Superseded by P.L. 119-21 Section 70306 ($4,000,000 phaseout threshold).

section_179_cap_2026.verbatim_quote: For taxable years beginning in 2026, the aggregate cost of any section 179 property that a taxpayer elects to treat as an expense cannot exceed $2,560,000.

superseded_values.label: 2024 Section 179 cap ($1,220,000)
superseded_values.reason: Outdated 2024 limit superseded for 2026 by IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32.

superseded_values.label: Pre-OBBBA 2025 Section 179 cap ($1,250,000)
superseded_values.reason: Superseded by P.L. 119-21 and IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32.

superseded_values.label: Pre-OBBBA projected 2026 Section 179 cap ($1,290,000)
superseded_values.reason: Superseded by P.L. 119-21 Section 70306 and IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32 ($2,560,000).

section_179_phaseout_2026.verbatim_quote: For taxable years beginning in 2026, the $2,560,000 section 179 dollar limitation is reduced by the amount by which the cost of section 179 property placed in service exceeds $4,090,000.

superseded_values.label: 2024 Section 179 phaseout ($3,050,000)
superseded_values.reason: Outdated 2024 threshold superseded by $4,090,000 for 2026.

superseded_values.label: Pre-OBBBA 2025 Section 179 phaseout ($3,130,000)
superseded_values.reason: Superseded by $4,090,000 for 2026 under IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32.

section_179_heavy_suv_cap_2025.verbatim_quote: For taxable years beginning in 2025, the cost of any sport utility vehicle that may be taken into account under section 179 cannot exceed $31,300.

section_179_heavy_suv_cap_2026.verbatim_quote: For taxable years beginning in 2026, the cost of any sport utility vehicle subject to section 179(b)(5)(A) that may be taken into account under section 179 cannot exceed $32,000.

superseded_values.label: 2024 Heavy SUV Section 179 cap ($30,500)
superseded_values.reason: Outdated 2024 SUV cap; 2026 cap is $32,000.

superseded_values.label: 2025 Heavy SUV Section 179 cap ($31,300)
superseded_values.reason: 2025 SUV cap superseded for 2026 by $32,000 under IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32.

superseded_values.label: General Equipment Cap ($2,560,000) misapplied to Heavy SUVs
superseded_values.reason: Heavy SUVs (6,000-14,000 lbs GVWR) are capped at $32,000 under IRC Section 179(b)(5)(A), not $2,560,000.

bonus_depreciation_pct_2026.verbatim_quote: Public Law 119-21 Section 70301 amends 26 U.S.C. 168(k) to permanently restore a 100 percent additional first-year bonus depreciation allowance for qualified property acquired and placed in service after January 19, 2025.

superseded_values.label: Pre-OBBBA TCJA 2026 phasedown (20%)
superseded_values.reason: The 20% 2026 phasedown was repealed by P.L. 119-21 Section 70301 restoring 100% bonus depreciation.

standard_deduction_2026_single.verbatim_quote: For taxable years beginning in 2026, the standard deduction under section 63(c)(2) is $16,100 for single individuals and married individuals filing separate returns.

superseded_values.label: Pre-OBBBA 2025 Single Standard Deduction ($15,000)
superseded_values.reason: 2025 pre-OBBBA figure superseded by $16,100 for 2026.

superseded_values.label: Pre-OBBBA 2026 projected Single Standard Deduction ($15,350)
superseded_values.reason: Superseded by P.L. 119-21 and IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32 ($16,100).

superseded_values.label: Repealed TCJA Sunset Single Standard Deduction ($8,600)
superseded_values.reason: TCJA sunset was repealed by P.L. 119-21.

standard_deduction_2026_mfj.verbatim_quote: For taxable years beginning in 2026, the standard deduction under section 63(c)(2) is $32,200 for married individuals filing joint returns and surviving spouses.

superseded_values.label: Pre-OBBBA 2025 MFJ Standard Deduction ($30,000)
superseded_values.reason: Superseded by $32,200 for 2026 under IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32.

standard_deduction_2026_hoh.verbatim_quote: For taxable years beginning in 2026, the standard deduction under section 63(c)(2) is $24,150 for heads of households.

tax_brackets_2026_single.verbatim_quote: For taxable years beginning in 2026, unmarried individuals (other than surviving spouses and heads of households) are subject to marginal rates of 10%, 12%, 22%, 24%, 32%, 35%, and 37% with thresholds at $12,400, $50,400, $105,700, $201,775, $256,225, and $640,600.

superseded_values.label: Pre-OBBBA / 2025 bracket thresholds ($12,050 / $48,900 / $104,400)

superseded_values.label: Repealed 39.6% TCJA sunset top rate

standard_deduction_2027_single.verbatim_quote: For taxable years beginning in 2027, the standard deduction under section 63(c)(2) rises to $16,600 for single individuals and married individuals filing separately.

superseded_values.label: Repealed TCJA Sunset Single Standard Deduction ($8,600)
superseded_values.reason: TCJA sunset was repealed by P.L. 119-21; 2027 single standard deduction is $16,600.

standard_deduction_2027_mfj.verbatim_quote: For taxable years beginning in 2027, the standard deduction under section 63(c)(2) rises to $33,200 for married couples filing jointly.

standard_deduction_2027_hoh.verbatim_quote: For taxable years beginning in 2027, the standard deduction under section 63(c)(2) rises to $24,925 for heads of households.

tax_brackets_2027_single.verbatim_quote: For taxable years beginning in 2027, unmarried single filers are subject to marginal tax rates of 10%, 12%, 22%, 24%, 32%, 35%, and 37% with thresholds at $12,800, $52,025, $109,125, $208,325, $264,550, and $661,375.

superseded_values.label: Repealed 39.6% TCJA sunset rate

qsbs_asset_ceiling_post_obbba.verbatim_quote: Public Law 119-21 Section 70431 increases the Qualified Small Business Stock aggregate gross asset ceiling from $50,000,000 to $75,000,000 for stock issued after July 4, 2025.

superseded_values.label: Legacy pre-July-4-2025 QSBS asset ceiling ($50,000,000)
superseded_values.reason: Applies only to QSBS issued on or before July 4, 2025; post-OBBBA stock ceiling is $75,000,000.

qsbs_exclusion_cap_post_obbba.verbatim_quote: Public Law 119-21 Section 70431 increases the per-issuer Section 1202 QSBS gain exclusion cap from $10,000,000 to $15,000,000 (or 10x basis) for stock acquired after July 4, 2025.

superseded_values.label: Legacy pre-July-4-2025 QSBS exclusion cap ($10,000,000)
superseded_values.reason: Legacy $10M cap applies only to stock acquired on or before July 4, 2025; post-OBBBA cap is $15,000,000.

qsbs_holding_tiers.verbatim_quote: For QSBS acquired after July 4, 2025 under P.L. 119-21 Section 70431, the applicable gain exclusion percentage is 50 percent for stock held at least 3 years, 75 percent for stock held at least 4 years, and 100 percent for stock held at least 5 years.

retirement_401k_2026.verbatim_quote: The annual elective deferral limit for employees participating in 401(k), 403(b), and most 457 plans for 2026 is $24,500.
